etymology: Pictograph: a bird climbing with both wings beating and neck stretched — to fly.
mnemonic: Mid-takeoff, feathers everywhere — とぶ. 飛行機 borrowed the wings; the kanji still owns them.

components: heart with a stake through it
etymology: Originally the bound haft of a weapon — 'fixed firm'; the shape later read as a heart pinned by a stroke: invariably, without fail.
mnemonic: A heart with a stake through it cannot change its mind — かならず. 必要, 必死: needs and resolves at 100%.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 票 (phonetic ヒョウ) — the marker at the treetop, visible far off: a sign, a mark.
mnemonic: The flag lashed to the tallest branch: aim here — ヒョウ. 目標: the branch your eyes keep returning to.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (寸) pressing something onto a person (亻) — to hand over, to attach.
mnemonic: Pressed into your palm until it sticks — つける. 受付 attaches visitors to the building; 気を付けて attaches care to you.

etymology: Pictograph: a grown man (大) with the pin of adulthood through his topknot (一) — a full-grown man: husband.
mnemonic: The pin through the hair says: adult, married, responsible — おっと. 大丈夫 stacks three sturdy kanji into 'it's fine'.

etymology: Phono-semantic: roof (宀) + 畐 'jar full to the brim' (phonetic フ) — abundance under the roof: wealth.
mnemonic: The pantry jar that never empties — とみ. 富士山: the mountain named like a full house.

etymology: Phono-semantic: building (广) + 付 (phonetic フ) — the government repository where documents attach: the seat of administration; today Osaka-fu, Kyoto-fu.
mnemonic: The building all the paperwork sticks to — フ. 政府: the biggest flypaper of all.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 畐 'full vessel' (phonetic フク) + blade (刂) — the vessel split to make a matching second: duplicate, deputy: vice-.
mnemonic: Slice the jar's contents into a twin copy — フク. 副社長: the copy that signs when the original is away.

etymology: Compound ideograph: an axe (斤) gripped in both hands — the armed man: soldier, troops.
mnemonic: Both fists on the axe-haft, ready — ヘイ. 兵士: the kanji is already at attention.

etymology: Simplified from 變: tangled threads beaten (攵) into a new state — to change; what changed too far: strange.
mnemonic: Beat the knot until it becomes something else — かわる; if it comes out weird, that's 変 too — へん.

etymology: Simplified from 邊: movement (辶) + a tall phonetic — where the road runs out: the edge, the vicinity.
mnemonic: Walk until the map frays — あたり, ベ. この辺: 'around here', measured in strolls.

etymology: Pictograph: a body curled around a fetus (勹 around 巳) — the original wrapping: to wrap, envelop.
mnemonic: Curled protectively around what's inside — つつむ. 包丁, oddly, is the kitchen knife: what unwraps dinner.

etymology: Compound: water (氵) + 去 — law like water: it finds its level everywhere it goes; the leveled way of doing: method.
mnemonic: Water settles perfectly flat, no exceptions granted — ホウ. 方法 is the路 of doing; 法律 the water applied to people.

etymology: Compound: a figure standing tall, gazing at the moon (月) for what is absent (亡) — longing, hope; the moon gazed at fullest: full moon.
mnemonic: On tiptoe, eyes on the full moon, wanting — のぞむ. 希望: hope with its neck craned.

etymology: Ideograph: a tree (木) with a long stroke marking its topmost branch — the far end: the tip, the close. Mirror of 本, which marks the root.
mnemonic: The mark at the treetop: as far as it goes — すえ. 週末: the branch-tip of the week.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 㒼 (phonetic マン) — filled level to the rim: full, complete.
mnemonic: Poured to the brim without one drop over — みちる. 満員: a train filled by the same principle.

etymology: Ideograph: a tree (木) whose top branch is still short — growth unfinished: not yet. Twin of 末, where the branch has arrived.
mnemonic: The upper branch hasn't caught up: unfinished — ミ. 未来: the not-yet, scheduled; 未満: not yet reaching the line.

etymology: Pictograph of a dancer with tasseled sleeves, borrowed since the oracle bones for 'there is not' — the dots below are the deformed legs, not fire.
mnemonic: The dance ends, the stage is bare — ない, ム. 無料 is 'nothing owed'; 無理 'no way there'.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 勺 (phonetic ヤク) — a cord knotted at the agreed measure: a promise; measured, not exact: approximately.
mnemonic: Tie the knot where you both agreed — ヤク. 約束 doubles the binding; 約3時間 keeps the knot loose.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 甬 (phonetic ユウ) + strength (力) — strength welling up and through: courage.
mnemonic: The strength that moves before fear finishes talking — いさむ. 勇気: the kanji that goes first.

etymology: Pictograph: hands gripping a waist (the root of 腰) — the body's pivot point: the essential; what the essential does: need.
mnemonic: Everything above and below turns on the waist — いる, ヨウ. 必要: pinned and pivotal at once.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 谷 'valley' (phonetic ヨク) — stepping into the valley stream: to bathe, to bask.
mnemonic: The mountain pours a private shower into the ravine — あびる. 浴衣: what you wear walking back from it.

etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) + blade (刂) — the sickle slicing clean through the harvest: sharp; what the harvest yields: profit, advantage.
mnemonic: A sharp edge cuts more grain per swing — リ. 便利 is life with good edges; 利益 the grain they bring in.

etymology: Phono-semantic: mound (阝) + 坴 (phonetic リク) — high dry ground: land, as opposed to sea.
mnemonic: Dirt piled on dirt until the sea gives up — リク. 大陸: the pile at continental scale; 陸上: sports on it.

etymology: Pictograph: a sifting device separating fine grain from chaff — what passes the sieve: good.
mnemonic: Only the best grains make it through — よい. 良い is the sieve's verdict; 奈良 wears it in its name.

etymology: Pictograph: a grain sack with a measuring opening at the top — to measure out: quantity.
mnemonic: The sack tells you how much by the mouthful — リョウ. 大量, measure overflowing; 測量, measuring gone professional.

etymology: Phono-semantic: cart (車) + 侖 'ordered arrangement' (phonetic リン) — spokes set in perfect order: the wheel; any ring.
mnemonic: Spokes filed in a circle like books on a round shelf — わ. 指輪 for the finger, 五輪 for the Olympics.

etymology: Phono-semantic: a phonetic built of rice and dog + head (頁) — things whose 'heads' resemble each other, sorted into heaps: kind, sort.
mnemonic: Sort the pantry by lookalikes: this heap, that heap — ルイ. 種類: heaps with labels; 書類: heaps with staples.

etymology: Compound ideograph: the assembly summoned (亼) and one kneeling (卩) to receive the word — a command, a decree.
mnemonic: The scroll read from the steps, everyone on one knee — レイ. 命令: orders with your name on them; 令和: an era named by one.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 列 'row' (phonetic レイ) — people lined up as precedents: an example, a custom.
mnemonic: Pull one person out of the line to show the rest — たとえば. 例えば: the kanji clearing its throat before a for-instance.

etymology: Phono-semantic: ice (冫) + 令 (phonetic レイ) — cold as a decree: chilled, cool (of things and of people).
mnemonic: Orders delivered over ice — つめたい. 冷蔵庫 keeps the beer 冷たい; some replies come out of the same drawer.

etymology: Compound ideograph: carts (車) moving (辶) coupled in a train — linked one to the next: to connect, to take along.
mnemonic: Wagon hitched to wagon, all rolling together — つれる. 連絡 links people; 連休 links holidays.

etymology: Simplified from 勞: fires blazing above strength (力) — strength burned through the night: labor, toil.
mnemonic: Working by torchlight until the fuel is you — ロウ. 苦労 is the invoice; ご苦労さま the receipt.

etymology: Pictograph: an elder with long hair bent over a cane — old age.
mnemonic: Hair grown past the shoulders, weight on the stick — おいる. 老人: the kanji leaning as it walks.

etymology: Phono-semantic: metal (金) + 彔 (phonetic ロク) — cut into bronze so it cannot be unsaid: to record.
mnemonic: Engraved, not jotted — ロク. 記録 outlives the writer; 録音 does it to sound.

etymology: Simplified from 壓: the cliff's mass (厂) bearing down on the earth (土) — crushing weight: pressure.
mnemonic: The whole cliff resting on one patch of ground — アツ. 気圧 is the sky doing it; プレッシャー the boss's version.

etymology: Phono-semantic (simplified from 圍): enclosure (囗) + 井 (phonetic イ) — walls drawn around: to surround.
mnemonic: The village well with a fence on all four sides — かこむ. 周囲: everything inside your fence-line of attention.

etymology: Pictograph read as a lizard that changes color — change (the 易 of the I Ching); what changes without resistance: easy.
mnemonic: The lizard switches colors without effort — やさしい, エキ. 貿易 is nations doing the color-swap; 簡単より易しい.

etymology: Phono-semantic: grain (禾) + 多 (phonetic イ) — seedlings transplanted bed to bed: to shift, transfer.
mnemonic: Rice moved seedling by seedling to the big paddy — うつる. 移動: the transplant, applied to yourself.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a person (大) lying on the mat (囗) that supports them — the thing an outcome rests on: cause, basis.
mnemonic: Whatever you find under the result when you lift it — イン. 原因: the mat the accident was lying on.

etymology: Simplified from 營: watchfires over connected quarters (呂) — the laid-out camp; to run its operations: to operate, manage.
mnemonic: Lamps burning over both offices — えいぎょう中. 営業: the fires are lit, come in.

etymology: Pictograph: a river shown with its long branching course — water that runs on and on: eternal.
mnemonic: One drop more than 水: enough to run forever — ながい, エイ. 永遠: the river with no last bend.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 夜 (phonetic エキ) — flowing substance: liquid, fluid.
mnemonic: Water that works the night shift in your body — エキ. 血液: the busiest fluid on the payroll.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 寅 (phonetic エン) — water drawn out long: to extend, unfold; to unfold before an audience: to perform.
mnemonic: Let the idea flow out at full length under the lights — エン. 演説 unfolds words; 演技 unfolds a role.
